candidate1_reference.role: historical scientific evidence only; not a Candidate 2 tuning target

estimand.population: Synthetic subjects in the declared 21-day observation population with an observable treatment/outcome record under the declared measurement condition.
estimand.treatment_or_exposure: Binary presence versus absence of one focal synthetic channel exposure before the qualifying outcome/horizon.
estimand.outcome: Qualifying conversion within the 21-day observation horizon.
estimand.intervention: Set the focal channel exposure indicator to present while retaining the subject's declared observable non-focal exposure/history covariates as the controlled background regime.
estimand.comparison: Set the same focal channel exposure indicator to absent under the same declared observable covariate pattern.
estimand.temporal_ordering: Only information observable before the qualifying outcome or end of horizon may enter treatment, outcome or adjustment features.
estimand.treatment_regime: One-channel-at-a-time static binary intervention under the declared observed background treatment/history regime.
estimand.aggregation_target: Population-average signed conversion-probability difference for each synthetic channel.

observable_adjustment_variables: normalized timing summaries computed from observable pre-outcome touches
identification_assumptions: Conditional exchangeability given the declared observable adjustment variables.
Positivity/overlap for focal-channel treatment after conditioning on the declared observables.
Consistency of the declared binary channel intervention.
The controlled background exposure/history regime is a scientifically acceptable conditioning set for this synthetic estimand.
At least one nuisance model is sufficiently specified for the doubly robust estimating equation under the identification assumptions.
scientific_limit: Doubly robust does not mean robust to unobserved confounding. If important latent intent remains unobserved and exchangeability fails, Candidate 2 may remain biased even when one nuisance model is correctly specified.
uncertainty_target: Approximate 90% influence-function interval for each population-average channel effect, with interval calibration evaluated by the external evaluator.

hypothesis.statement: An interpretable doubly robust estimator combining an outcome model with a treatment-propensity model may reduce synthetic bias from observed treatment-selection mechanisms relative to the frozen Candidate 1 outcome-regression estimator while retaining signed effects and calibrated uncertainty, provided the causal identification assumptions hold and at least one nuisance model is sufficiently specified.
falsifiable_failure_conditions: both nuisance models are materially misspecified
measurement loss removes necessary confounders or exposure information
interactions or time variation exceed the declared model structure
numerical instability produces invalid propensity or effect estimates

prohibited_uses: Candidate 1 sealed-holdout family MAEs as development targets
Candidate 1 sealed-holdout coverage values as tuning targets
candidate1_holdout_restriction.allowed_use: Only the general scientific questions of observable treatment selection, known-zero behavior, hidden confounding/latent intent and uncertainty calibration may motivate Candidate 2.

public_holdout_limitation_disclosure: The holdout-family architecture is public because the repository is public. The instantiated holdout seeds, parameter values, treatment effects, latent-intent strengths, interactions, selection mechanisms and corruption settings remain sealed from Candidate 2 development. This is strong research-process separation, not a completely secret external benchmark.
